# Destroying a Data-worker Pipeline calls an unavailable proxy method

## Context

An isolated Chrome 156.0.8078.80 probe of a plain `telemetry:false` Pipeline used the actual App and Data workers. Its read executed in Data and returned correctly; `Pipeline.destroy()` then threw `TypeError: Neo.worker.Data.sendMessage is not a function`.

The same failure occurs with the `origin/dev` Pipeline from `f82061f2c94d286a6e6c080f9e63cd17a266797b` (blob `f7cd4f01f4ce9d8a6e7512b075e5eadcc5360d3a`) served at its actual module URL. This predates the opt-in telemetry work in #9554 / PR #20434. The browser used `useAiClient:false`; no Brain, Neural Link or shared store was connected.

## The Problem

Once a Pipeline has a Data-side `remoteId`, its destroy branch calls `sendMessage` on `Neo.worker.Data`. In the App realm that object is the Data worker's remote API, which exposes `createInstance`, `loadDataModule` and `loadModule`; `sendMessage` is undefined. The throw prevents the rest of Pipeline's ordinary disposal.

Design authority: `Pipeline#destroy` already intends to send `destroyInstance` for its counterpart, and `worker.Data#onDestroyInstance` already owns disposal and removal from its `instances` map. This restores that existing lifecycle, without adding a disposal API.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/data/Pipeline.mjs#initRemoteExecution` creates the counterpart through the Data remote API.
- `src/data/Pipeline.mjs#destroy` dispatches to the wrong object.
- `src/worker/Data.mjs#onDestroyInstance` destroys the instance and removes its retained entry.
- The App worker's `Neo.currentWorker` owns outgoing worker messages.

A source-substitution control changed only `Neo.worker.Data.sendMessage({` to `Neo.currentWorker.sendMessage('data', {`. With distinct App/Data IDs, the plain read still passed; destroy removed the App registry entry and eventually both the Data `instances` entry and `Neo.get(remoteId)`. No page or console errors occurred. This proves observed cleanup, not a new awaited acknowledgement contract.

## The Fix

Route the existing destruction message through its existing worker-message owner. Preserve stage disposal, ordinary local Pipelines, and Base's duplicate-destroy guard. Pin both the negative baseline and actual receiver cleanup; a call-count-only mock is insufficient.

Prescription checked independently by Grace at dev f82061f2c9: `src/data/Pipeline.mjs` owns the sender; existing `Data#onDestroyInstance` owns removal. The same coherent disposal leaf also covers destruction while normal creation is in flight: stop before creation after a destroyed preload, or dispose a successful late creation reply without publishing state onto the destroyed App instance. This adds no acknowledgement or pending-operation settlement contract.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback / limit | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remote Pipeline disposal | Existing `Pipeline#destroy` and `Data#onDestroyInstance` | Connected counterpart receives its captured ID and is removed; App disposal completes | No new promise/acknowledgement or worker-failure recovery contract | Method JSDoc | Unit dispatch and native distinct-ID cleanup controls |
| Local disposal | `Pipeline#destroy` and `core.Base` | Existing stage cleanup and duplicate-destroy suppression remain | No Data dispatch without a remote counterpart | Existing lifecycle docs | Local and repeated-destroy controls |

Decision Record impact: none — restoration through the existing App/Data boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit control is red on the baseline and verifies dispatch through the App worker message owner with the exact counterpart ID.
- [ ] A native App/Data control with distinct IDs completes disposal and observes removal from the App registry, Data `instances` map and Data registry; profiling is off.
- [ ] Local Pipelines, owned stage cleanup and duplicate-destroy suppression remain correct. Destruction during preload must prevent creation; a creation reply after disposal must release its returned Data ID without resurrecting App state. Pin both with controlled promises and the latter through actual App/Data receivers.

## Out of Scope

Telemetry, backend record deletion, new remote methods, async disposal acknowledgements, worker-restart recovery and unrelated Store/Application lifecycle changes.

## Avoided Traps

Do not add a `sendMessage` shim to the Data remote API or bypass its existing receiver. Do not treat closing the entire browser as proof of per-instance disposal.
